questions.question: What is Minitest and how do you write a test in it?
questions.title: Minitest Basics
questions.direct_answer: Minitest is Ruby's default, fast, small testing library (bundled with Ruby; Rails' default). A test is a method starting with `test_` in a class inheriting from `Minitest::Test` (or `ActiveSupport::TestCase` in Rails): `class UserTest < Minitest::Test; def test_valid; assert User.new(name: 'Al').valid?; end; end`. Assertions: `assert` (truthy), `assert_equal` (expected == actual), `assert_nil`, `assert_raises(Errno) { ... }`, `refute` (falsy). Run with `ruby -Ilib -e 'require "minitest/autorun"; require "user_test"'` or `bin/rails test`. Specs style: `describe User do; it 'is valid' do; assert ...; end; end`. Fixtures load YAML data. Minitest values smallness/speed and ships with Ruby; RSpec is larger and more expressive but an extra dependency. For a fresh Rails app, Minitest is the default — use it unless your team prefers RSpec.

Assertions: assert (truthy), assert equal (expected equals actual), assert nil, assert raises Errno do dot dot dot end, refute (falsy). Run with ruby minus Ilib minus e (require minitest autorun; require user test) or bin rails test. Specs style: describe User do; it is valid do; assert dot dot dot; end; end. Fixtures load YAML data. sections.title: Minitest
sections.content:
Ruby's default test lib. class < Minitest::Test; def test_x; assert/assert_equal. Fast, bundled. bin/rails test.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[class UserTest < Minitest::Test] --> T[def test_valid]
  T --> A[assert/assert_equal]
  R[bin/rails test] --> F[runs all tests]
```

sections.title: Minitest
sections.content:
```ruby
require 'minitest/autorun'
require 'minitest/pride'           # colored output

class UserTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_valid                    # methods starting with 'test_'
    user = User.new(name: 'Al')
    assert user.valid?              # truthy
  end

  def test_name_required
    user = User.new(name: '')
    refute user.valid?              # falsy
    assert_equal ["can't be blank"], user.errors[:name]
  end

  def test_raises_on_bad_id
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound) { User.find(999_999) }
  end
end

# In Rails (ActiveSupport::TestCase adds fixtures, etc.):
class UserTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  # fixtures :all                 # load YAML from test/fixtures/
  test 'is valid with a name' do  # 'test' helper = def test_is_valid...
    assert User.new(name: 'Al').valid?
  end
end

# Common assertions:
#   assert x           -> x truthy
#   assert_equal a, b  -> a == b
#   assert_nil x
#   refute x           -> x falsy
#   assert_raises(ErrorClass) { ... }
#   assert_in_delta 1.0, 1.01, 0.1   -> within tolerance

# Spec style (minitest/autorun + minitest/spec):
require 'minitest/autorun'
describe User do
  it 'is valid' do
    assert User.new(name: 'Al').valid?
  end
end

# Run:
#   bin/rails test                    # all
#   bin/rails test test/models/user_test.rb  # one file
#   bin/rails test test/models/user_test.rb:10  # one line
#   ruby -Ilib -e 'require "minitest/autorun"; require "./test/user_test"'

# Minitest is small, fast, bundled with Ruby. RSpec is richer but an extra gem.
```
